flashcards.definition: Single layer of flattened pavement cells; lines blood vessel endothelium, peritoneal mesothelium, and lung alveoli.
Cube-like cells with central spherical nuclei; lines thyroid follicles, salivary gland ducts, and germinal ovary surface.
Simple cuboidal cells with microvilli lining the PCT of renal nephron for maximum absorption.
Tall pillar-like cells with oval basal nuclei; lines stomach, intestine mucosa, and gall bladder.
Unicellular exocrine mucus-secreting glands interspersed within columnar epithelium of GI and respiratory tracts.
Single cell layer of varying heights appearing multi-layered; ciliated variant lines trachea and large bronchi.
Multi-layered compound epithelium covered by dead keratinized stratum corneum; forms epidermis of dry skin.
Multi-layered living surface cells lining moist membranes: oral cavity, pharynx, oesophagus, vagina, cornea.
Distensible plastic compound epithelium with pear-shaped/umbrella surface cells lining urinary bladder and ureters.
Occluding junctions that fuse adjacent cell membranes, preventing fluid leakage across epithelial barriers.
Button-like anchoring junctions coupled to keratin intermediate filaments that resist severe mechanical shear.
Communicating channel junctions formed by connexon proteins allowing ion and second-messenger passage.
Exocrine glands retain ducts to secrete enzymes/mucus; Endocrine glands are ductless, releasing hormones into blood.
Merocrine (exocytosis e.g. sweat), Apocrine (apical loss e.g. mammary), Holocrine (cell breakdown e.g. sebaceous).
